symptom: High traffic, low conversion
diagnostic_check: Buyer vs. user mismatch, or wrong stage of the buying process is being targeted.

symptom: CAC rising across all channels
diagnostic_check: Segment no longer passes the accessibility/profitability tests — re-run segmentation.

symptom: Revenue flat despite ad spend increase
diagnostic_check: Check reach/frequency/CPM efficiency and whether the product has entered the maturity or decline stage of the PLC.

symptom: Margin erosion at scale
diagnostic_check: Audit channel margins and slotting/distribution costs, not just unit economics.

symptom: "We're profitable but cash-strapped"
diagnostic_check: Reconcile accrual net income against the cash flow statement — check receivables aging and working capital, not the income statement.

symptom: Margins look fine but the ratio dashboard is flashing red
diagnostic_check: Separate liquidity, leverage, profitability, and efficiency ratios — a healthy margin can mask a liquidity or turnover problem.

symptom: Leadership wants to greenlight a project on "gut feel"
diagnostic_check: Require NPV/IRR against the company's WACC (see Part III) before recommending go/no-go.

symptom: Stakeholder wants to fund a pet project
diagnostic_check: Ask for the NPV and IRR against WACC before committing analytics resources to support it.

symptom: A/B test or pilot shows a promising but noisy result
diagnostic_check: Report variance and standard deviation alongside the mean — don't let a single expected value stand alone.

symptom: Leadership compares options only on payback period
diagnostic_check: Reintroduce NPV/IRR — payback ignores everything that happens after the money is recovered.

symptom: Great dashboard, nobody uses it
diagnostic_check: Check job design (was it built for the actual decision-maker's autonomy and workflow?) and expectancy theory (do users believe using it changes an outcome they care about?).

symptom: Team agrees too quickly on a flawed data story
diagnostic_check: Groupthink — deliberately assign a devil's-advocate review before finalizing analysis for leadership.

symptom: A data-driven change keeps getting rolled back
diagnostic_check: Diagnose it as a change-management failure (skipped unfreeze/refreeze), not a data quality failure.

symptom: Total output isn't improving despite upgrades in several process steps
diagnostic_check: You improved a non-bottleneck step. Re-identify the true bottleneck before investing further.

symptom: Defect/error rate is inconsistent and unpredictable
diagnostic_check: Apply SPC — separate common-cause variation (expected, systemic) from special-cause variation (a specific, fixable event).

symptom: Inventory (or backlog) is either piling up or constantly running out
diagnostic_check: Recheck EOQ inputs — demand, order cost, and holding cost assumptions may be stale.

symptom: A KPI declines across every account/segment simultaneously
diagnostic_check: Rule out a macro driver (rates, inflation, demand shock) before diagnosing an internal cause.

symptom: Leadership asks "why are we losing share"
diagnostic_check: Rebuild the perceptual map with current pricing/quality data before proposing tactics — the positioning may have drifted, not the execution.

symptom: A cross-functional initiative stalls
diagnostic_check: Check strategic fit — operations, marketing, and pricing may be optimizing for different generic strategies (e.g., ops for cost leadership while marketing sells on premium differentiation).

symptom: A "synergy" business case doesn't materialize in the numbers
diagnostic_check: Verify the underlying shared resource (customers, tech, skills) actually overlaps — synergy claims without a concrete shared asset rarely show up in the data.

symptom: Analysis is technically correct but rejected by stakeholders
diagnostic_check: Reconsider the delivery — was it persuasion-balanced (logic/credibility/emotion), or purely logic-heavy?

symptom: Two teams keep disagreeing on the same metric definition
diagnostic_check: Treat it as a negotiation — find the ZOPA on the metric definition rather than re-litigating from scratch each time.

symptom: A partner or vendor wants data used outside its original agreement
diagnostic_check: Treat it as a contract/IP question first — check the consideration and scope of the original agreement before proceeding.

symptom: A model or report could materially mislead a decision-maker
diagnostic_check: Apply the ethical decision-making steps before shipping — this is a governance issue, not just a QA issue.

symptom: Two valuation methods for the same target disagree sharply
diagnostic_check: Expected — reconcile them in a football field rather than picking one; a large DCF-vs-comps gap usually means the DCF's growth or terminal value assumptions need re-stress-testing against what the market is actually paying.

symptom: A proposed acquisition grows revenue but leadership is still nervous
diagnostic_check: Run the accretion/dilution math — top-line growth alone doesn't tell you whether EPS, and therefore likely market reaction, improves or worsens.

symptom: A private equity-style investment case looks attractive on IRR alone
diagnostic_check: Check how much of that IRR is coming from leverage (financial engineering) versus actual EBITDA growth (operational value creation) — the mix matters for how repeatable the return is.

symptom: Resolution time is rising but ticket volume is flat
diagnostic_check: Check backlog growth, escalation rate, and staffing per agent first; then check whether one ticket category or team explains it.

symptom: Customers complain but satisfaction scores look fine
diagnostic_check: Check who answers the survey (response bias) and whether reopened tickets or repeat contacts show hidden dissatisfaction.

symptom: On-time performance (late flights) is dropping at one airport
diagnostic_check: Split delay minutes by cause first; then check taxi-out time, turnaround time, and late inbound aircraft at that airport.

symptom: Delays (late flights) pile up later in the day
diagnostic_check: Check delay propagation from late inbound aircraft and short turnaround buffers before blaming local causes.

symptom: Safety event counts are rising while flying activity also rises
diagnostic_check: Convert counts to rates per exposure (flight hours or departures) before judging the trend.

symptom: Report counts jumped after a safety campaign
diagnostic_check: A rise in voluntary reports can mean a healthier reporting culture, not more hazards; compare report rate with hazard severity.

symptom: Dashboard numbers disagree between teams
diagnostic_check: Check metric definitions and data freshness before debating results; align on one definition and one source.

symptom: A metric moved sharply right after a system or pipeline change
diagnostic_check: Check pipeline failures and completeness around the change date before treating the move as real.
